\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Fourier Theory of Threshold Functions}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.Fourier
\section{Overview}
This chapter relates polynomial threshold representations to Fourier uniqueness, low-degree spectral weight, noise sensitivity, and sparsity. It also records the flat spectrum and threshold sparsity of inner product modulo two, together with uniform sparse polynomial approximations.
\section{Declarations}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and let $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be $\pm1$-valued functions.
Suppose $f$ is represented as the threshold sign of a multilinear polynomial of degree
at most $k$, with zero assigned sign $1$, and suppose $f$ and $g$ have equal
Fourier–Walsh coefficients at every subset of coordinates of cardinality at most $k$.
Then $g=f$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be $\pm1$-valued. Suppose $f$ is
a polynomial threshold function of degree at most one. If their Fourier–Walsh
coefficients agree at every subset $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $|S|\le1$, then
$g=f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Exponential decay beyond a reciprocal scale]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.one_sub_two_mul_pow_le_third}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $\delta\in\mathbb R$ and $m\in\mathbb N$. If $\delta\le\tfrac12$ and $1<\delta m$,
then
\[
(1-2\delta)^m\le\frac13.
\]
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in $\{-1,1\}$. If
$0<\delta\le\tfrac12$, then the Fourier weight on levels strictly greater than
$\lfloor\delta^{-1}\rfloor$ is at most three times the noise sensitivity at parameter
$\delta$; here the Fourier weight is computed with uniform measure, and noise
sensitivity is defined by
$\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f)=\bigl(1-\operatorname{Stab}_{1-2\delta}(f)\bigr)/2$ using
the Fourier noise operator.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Approximation by a low degree threshold function]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.close_to_low_degree_ptf}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsClose, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsPolynomialThreshold, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.threshold, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.disagreementProbability, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.expect_mono, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightAbove, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightAbove_le_three_mul_noiseSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.noiseSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.thresholdSign, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne, KKL.l2DistSq, KKL.lowDegreePart, KKL.lowDegree_l2_error}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p115-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p115-b008
}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be $\pm1$-valued, and let
$0<\delta\le\tfrac12$. There is a function $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ that is a
polynomial threshold function of degree at most $\lfloor\delta^{-1}\rfloor$ and whose
uniform probability of disagreement with $f$ is at most $3\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f)$,
where $\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f)$ is the noise sensitivity defined using the Fourier
noise operator.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Bound on the mean absolute polynomial value]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sq_expect_abs_le_mul_fourierWeightUpTo}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsPolynomialThresholdRepresentation, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.expect_abs_eval_eq_innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.innerProduct_eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightUpTo, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $p$ be a real coefficient family indexed by subsets of $[n]$,
and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. Suppose $p(S)=0$ whenever $|S|>k$, and $f(x)$ is the
threshold sign of $\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}p(S)\chi_S(x)$, with sign $1$ at nonnegative
values and $-1$ at negative values. Then, for uniform expectation on the cube,
$\bigl(\mathbb
E|\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}p(S)\chi_S(x)|\bigr)^2\le\bigl(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}p(S)^2\bigr)\bigl(\sum_{|S|\le
k}\widehat f(S)^2\bigr)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Fourier weight of a zero polynomial threshold]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightUpTo_of_rep_zero}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsPolynomialThresholdRepresentation, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.threshold, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightUpTo, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.fourier_coeff_chi}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and suppose $f$ is the threshold
function represented by the identically zero multilinear polynomial, with threshold sign
equal to $1$ at zero. Then the Fourier weight of $f$ on levels at most $k$ is $1$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Norm bounds imply low-degree Fourier weight]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.le_fourierWeightUpTo_of_l1_l2}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsPolynomialThreshold, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.sum_sq_pos, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightUpTo, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightUpTo_of_rep_zero, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sq_expect_abs_le_mul_fourierWeightUpTo, BooleanAnalysis.expect}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $c\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
$c\le1$. Suppose $f$ is the threshold sign of a multilinear polynomial of degree at most
$k$. Suppose also that every coefficient family $p$ of degree at most $k$ satisfies
\[c\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}p(S)^2\le\left(\mathbb E_x\left|\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}p(S)\chi_S(x)\right|\right)^2,\]
where $x$ is uniform on the Boolean cube and $\chi_S$ is the Walsh character. Then
$c\le\sum_{|S|\le k}\widehat f(S)^2$, the Fourier weight of $f$ on levels at most $k$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Linear thresholds retain half their weight]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.ltf_low_degree_weight}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsLinearThreshold, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.affine_khintchine_sq, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightUpTo, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.le_fourierWeightUpTo_of_l1_l2, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p114-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p115-b002
}
\difficulty{2}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ satisfy $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(a_\varnothing+\sum_{i=1}^na_i(-1)^{x_i})$ for real coefficients, where $\operatorname{sgn}(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$.
Define $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\chi_S(x)]$ for uniform $x$ and $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$; then
\[
 \frac12\le\sum_{|S|\le1}\widehat f(S)^2.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial thresholds retain exponential weight]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.ptf_low_degree_weight}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsPolynomialThreshold, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.fourierWeightUpTo, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.le_fourierWeightUpTo_of_l1_l2, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.low_degree_l1_l2_sq, BooleanAnalysis.isPmOne}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p116-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p116-b005
}
\difficulty{2}
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ for $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$.
Suppose $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(\sum_{|S|\le k}a_S\chi_S(x))$ for real coefficients, where $\operatorname{sgn}(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$, and define $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x[f(x)\chi_S(x)]$ using uniform expectation.
Then
\[
 e^{-2k}\le\sum_{|S|\le k}\widehat f(S)^2.
\]
\end{theorem}

  {context}

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p017-b007}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $p$ be a nonzero multilinear
polynomial on the Boolean cube whose threshold sign, with zero assigned sign $1$, is
$f$. If $F$ is a finite family of coordinate subsets containing every subset with
nonzero coefficient in $p$, then $1\leq\sum_{S\in F}|\widehat f(S)|$, where $\widehat
f(S)$ is the Fourier–Walsh coefficient of $f$ at $S$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be $\pm1$-valued, and let $p$ be a
nonzero multilinear polynomial on the Boolean cube whose threshold sign, with zero
assigned sign $1$, is $f$. If $F$ is a finite family of coordinate subsets containing
every subset with nonzero coefficient in $p$, then $1\leq\sum_{S\in F}|\widehat f(S)|$,
where $\widehat f(S)$ is the Fourier–Walsh coefficient of $f$ at $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Flat spectrum of inner product parity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.abs_fourierCoeff_innerProductModTwo}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BoolCube, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.innerProductModTwo, BooleanAnalysis.boolToSign, BooleanAnalysis.chiS, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.fourierCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.uniformWeight}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p117-b002}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and define $I:\{0,1\}^{2n}\to\{-1,1\}$ by $I(u,v)=(-1)^{\sum_{i=1}^nu_iv_i}$ for $u,v\in\{0,1\}^n$.
For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,2n\}$ define $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat I(S)=\mathbb E_x[I(x)\chi_S(x)]$ using uniform expectation; every such $S$ satisfies
\[
 |\widehat I(S)|=2^{-n}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Inner product parity requires exponential sparsity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.innerProductModTwo_ptf_sparsity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.IsPolynomialThresholdRepresentation, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.sparsity, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.support, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.abs_fourierCoeff_innerProductModTwo, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.innerProductModTwo, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.ptf_support_fourier_mass_of_ne_zero}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p117-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p117-b002
}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and define $I(u,v)=(-1)^{\sum_{i=1}^nu_iv_i}$ for $u,v\in\{0,1\}^n$.
Suppose the nonzero real multilinear polynomial $p(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,2n\}}a_S\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$, satisfies $I(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(p(x))$ for all $x\in\{0,1\}^{2n}$, with $\operatorname{sgn}(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$.
Then $p$ has at least $2^n$ nonzero coefficients: $2^n\le|\{S:a_S\ne0\}|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform approximation by a sparse polynomial]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.sparse_polynomial_approximation}
\leanok

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be nonzero. Write
$\widehat f(S)$ for its Fourier–Walsh coefficient at $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and set
$L=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}|\widehat f(S)|$. For every $\delta>0$ and nonnegative
integer $s$ satisfying $4nL^2/\delta^2\le s$, there is a multilinear polynomial
$q(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}a_S\chi_S(x)$ with at most $s$ nonzero coefficients
such that $|f(x)-q(x)|<\delta$ for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sparse polynomial threshold representation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.exists_sparse_ptf_representation}

\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ take values in
$\{-1,1\}$. Write $\widehat f(S)$ for its Fourier–Walsh coefficient at $S\subseteq[n]$,
and set $s=\lceil 4n(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|\widehat f(S)|)^2\rceil$. Then $f$ has a
polynomial threshold representation with at most $s$ nonzero Walsh coefficients, and it
is also the threshold sign of a sum of exactly $s$ signed Walsh characters, allowing
repeated characters.
\end{theorem}
